sentences.text: This dinosaur featured a long tail that was broad at the hip joint but tapered significantly toward the end.
Its forelimbs were specialized for grasping, whereas its hindlimbs bore the animal's full body weight.
The hands contained three movable fingers alongside a fourth digit that was fused inside the group.
Specimens of this juvenile species are estimated to have stood between 0.7 and 1 meter tall.
Adult individuals are believed to have reached a total length of approximately 3 meters.
The estimated mass for an average adult is about 50 kilograms.
The genus is defined by a partial skeleton of a young animal that was once thought to belong to Thecodontosaurus.
The fossil material used to describe this genus had been known in scientific literature since 1983.
The fossils were originally discovered in 1952 by Kermack and Robinson.
In 2003, Adam Yates named the species Thecodontosaurus caducus based on fossil material NHMUK PV RUP 24.
It is probable that Pantydraco walked bipedally.
Researchers consider Pantydraco to have been probably omnivorous, representing a transition from carnivory to herbivory.
The genus Pantydraco was established by Galton, Yates, and Kermack in 2007.
Pantydraco is classified within the superorder Dinosauria, order Saurischia, and suborder Sauropodomorpha.
Pantydraco is generally considered basal within Sauropodomorpha, closely related to Thecodontosaurus.
Pantydraco lived during the Late Triassic, approximately 204 million years ago in the Rhaetian stage, in what is now Europe.
The region where Pantydraco lived was a characteristic wetland during the Triassic period.
